top.title: 8 Sci-Fi Books That Get Even Better the Second Time You Read Them
top.description: Science fiction is a genre built on far-out ideas, strange new worlds, and scientific possibilities that can fundamentally change how we understand our own. Some of the most unforgettable sci-fi novels offer just as much intrigue on a second reading as they do on the first. Whether it's a carefully constructed mystery, an intricate timeline, or a seemingly insignificant detail that takes on entirely new meaning once you know the ending, such books reward readers willing to go back for another speculative look.

top.title: Slow Turnout At Kaduna Polling Unit As INEC Holds Mock Accreditation
top.description: There is a slow turnout at polling units 031 and 032 in Ungwan Boro, Sabon Tasha ward, in Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State, as there is little to suggest that the mock accreditation exercise set to hold today by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is taking place. As at the time of filing this report, at exactly 9:29 am , officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission were yet to be on ground to commence the exercise scheduled to commence by 8:3am. The only security presence observed is that of three personnel of the Nigeria Security CIVIL Defence Corps (NSCDC) There is also no presence of voters at the two polling units, raising questions about the level of preparedness and awareness ahead of the exercise. The situation contrasts with INEC’s earlier assurance of readiness for the mock election, which is designed to assess its operational capacity and the effectiveness of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System and result transmission technology ahead of the 2027 general elections. As at Friday night, when voting materials were distributed at the INEC office in Kaduna, the Administrative Secretary, Abba Yahaya, also assured the public of the Commission’s readiness for the mock election, expressing confidence in its preparedness to conduct the exercise. top.title: Doctor’s coat takes backseat as Maha’s Vedika Magar chases cricket dreams for Sikkim
top.description: MUMBAI: Not many would give up a settled career, especially one as a doctor, to pursue a sporting dream. Vedika Magar did just that to follow her passion for cricket. Last month, she took her first step towards realising that dream when she represented Sikkim in the Senior Women’s T20 Trophy. Her next target is to play for Mumbai. She has featured on the state’s probables list for the past three seasons but is yet to make the Mumbai 15. Vedika had always wanted to be a cricketer. However, lack of facilities in her hometown of Pandharpur meant that her opportunities were limited to playing tennis-ball cricket with boys in her neighbourhood. When it came to choosing between an engineering seat in Pune and a medical seat in Mumbai, she opted for the latter and enrolled at Grant Medical College. She arrived in Mumbai at 17, fell in love with the city and rediscovered her passion for cricket. In college, she first bowled with a leather ball while practising with the boys’ team. She later began training at the nets of the late Vidya Paradkar, a well-known coach on Mumbai’s maidans, at Cross Maidan. It was only after completing her internship that she was encouraged to take cricket seriously. “Dr Hemant Gupta, who worked in the department of medicine at JJ Hospital, saw me play and was impressed. He was the one who helped me find a club in the city,” the 26-yearold said. At 23, Vedika put her plans for postgraduate studies on hold and took up a job at JJ Hospital to continue her cricketing journey. Her efforts paid off when she made Mumbai’s list of 30 probables for the first time in 2024. “Juggling night shifts, training and matches took a toll on me. I had calcium deficiency and my health deteriorated,” recalls the left-arm spinner. She eventually had to choose between her job and cricket. This time, with her parents’ support, she chose the game.She also landed a role as team doctor with Delhi Capitals’ Women’s Premier League (WPL) outfit. The job helped her manage her expenses while giving her an opportunity to interact with top players and observe their preparation. But progress on the field remained elusive. Then, while browsing the web, she came across an advertisement for open trials for Sikkim. She decided to give it a shot and was rewarded with selection.

top.title: Lawal pledges more projects as APC Campaign visits Shinkafi
top.description: Governor seeks support for Tinubu, APC candidates ahead of 2027 polls Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has pledged to execute more development projects in Shinkafi Local Government Area as he canvassed support for the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. Lawal made the pledge on Friday during the APC Zamfara North campaign flag-off rally held at the Eid ground in Shinkafi. The rally attracted party chieftains, including the Director-General of the Tinubu/Shettima Presidential Campaign Council and former governor, Abdul’aziz Yari; another former governor, Mahmuda Aliyu Shinkafi; the state APC Chairman, Kabiru Moyi; and other party leaders. Tens of thousands of supporters reportedly welcomed the campaign entourage at the town’s entrance, chanting slogans in support of the party. Addressing the gathering, Lawal thanked the people of Shinkafi for their solidarity and warm reception, saying their support was encouraging. He said his administration had recorded achievements in education, healthcare, infrastructure and economic development. The governor disclosed that his administration had rehabilitated six primary healthcare centres, including facilities in Badarawa, Birnin Yero, Galadi, Jangeru and Kurya. He described the ongoing referral hospital project in Shinkafi as a legacy initiative that would transform healthcare delivery in Zamfara State and the North-West. According to him, the project is central to his administration’s commitment to improving access to quality healthcare. Lawal also said his administration had completed 22 of the 31 projects undertaken over the past three and a half years, while the remaining nine were at more than 80 per cent completion. He urged residents to support President Bola Tinubu, his administration and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. “I am here once again to seek your votes. Vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, vote for me, and vote for the APC from top to bottom in the upcoming 2027 general election,” he said. The governor’s spokesman, Sulaiman Bala Idris, disclosed this in a statement issued on November 27, 2026. top.description: San Antonio Spurs guard Stephon Castle (5) celebrates after scoring a three-pointer in an NBA Cup game against the Los Angeles Lakers at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. The Spurs defeated the Lakers 99-96. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) The Spurs stressed at the start of NBA Cup play they wanted to win the in-season tournament after falling short in the championship game last season in Las Vegas. "We have our eyes on the prize, for sure." After overcoming a 20-point deficit to down the Los Angeles Lakers 99-96 on Friday night , the Spurs are one step closer to achieving that goal. top.title: Liverpool ready to battle to sign Bundesliga midfielder
top.description: Liverpool ready to battle to sign Bundesliga midfielder Liverpool transfer interest grows as Wael Mohya emerges as a summer market target Liverpool are among the clubs tracking Borussia Monchengladbach teenager Wael Mohya, with the 17-year-old German playmaker shaping up as one of the most intriguing young names to watch heading into the summer window. According to talkSPORT , Bayern Munich, Brighton and Barcelona are also credited with interest, a detail that immediately points to the level of competition any suitor is likely to face. Mohya’s rise has come against a difficult backdrop. Borussia Monchengladbach have endured a miserable Bundesliga campaign and, as reported, sit rooted to the bottom with only one league win all season. In that environment, young players can often be overwhelmed. Mohya has done the opposite. He has stepped in, handled senior football and contributed two goals in eight appearances, underlining why his name is now travelling so quickly across Europe. Wael Mohya making an impact in Germany There is already a sense that Mohya’s emergence is about more than numbers. He has also been recognised at international level after being named in the latest Germany squad, another marker of how highly he is regarded. He did not feature, but the selection alone signals serious belief in his potential. The player himself has attempted to dampen the noise. Mohya said: “If there were interest, it would be nice recognition of my performances, but nothing more than that. Just let me play football.” It is a measured response and one that suggests a teenager focused on development rather than headlines. That calm stance may be tested if Borussia Monchengladbach are relegated. Should that happen, the pressure to sell prized assets will inevitably increase. For interested clubs, that could create a rare opening to move for a talent before his valuation climbs even further. Photo: IMAGO Liverpool face Bayern Munich competition The expectation from those close to the German game is that the chase could quickly intensify. Andy Brassell told talkSPORT.com: “I think the fact that Mohya has been able to make an impression shows what an enormous personality he’s got.” That point matters. Scouts will always assess technique, output and tactical profile, but mentality is often what separates a promising youngster from a future elite operator. Brassell added: “He’s braver on the ball than a lot of his teammates. He wants to get the ball, he wants to take guys on, he wants to shoot.” It is easy to see why that description would appeal to recruitment departments across Europe, particularly clubs seeking creativity between the lines and confidence in tight spaces. He went further, saying: “Straight away it’s clear that he’s a pretty special talent.” In the current market, those judgments can accelerate quickly from admiration to active pursuit, especially when elite clubs sense a chance to act before a player becomes unattainable. top.title: The ‘extra spice’ fuelling France vs South Africa showdown in Nations Championship final
top.description: It is, in the words of a rival head coach, a “fitting final”. Andy Farrell did not hide his disappointment that Ireland did not make the inaugural Nations Championship showpiece but he did not dispute that France and South Africa were worthy combatants for the trophy. Asked to assess their relative strengths and make a prediction following his side’s win over Australia , the Ireland head coach spent several minutes explaining what makes each so good before eventually suggesting it was too close to call. “But isn’t that how it should be?” Farrell asked – indeed, Andy, indeed. This format clearly has its challenges but there is hope of a dazzling denouement. These are the reigning champions of the northern and southern hemispheres, however distant the Springboks ’ success in last year’s Rugby Championship now feels. Their recent encounter of fine margins in Paris has only deepened a rivalry that has festered in the last half-decade. “I find that it's a good challenge to play them twice in a row knowing that we have already beaten them the first time,” the France lock Florian Verhaeghe said. “That adds a little extra spice.” Florian Verhaeghe believes there will be ‘extra spice’ in the final (Getty) France, by rights, should not really be here. As detailed previously , they were more ambivalent than most towards the Nations Championship, with the July Test window generally considered secondary to the Top 14 climax that almost directly precedes it. Though Bordeaux Begles’ surprise failure to make the play-offs bolstered his options somewhat, head coach Fabien Galthie was still without a raft of regulars for fixtures against New Zealand, Australia and Japan in the first phase of this tournament; to come away with 12 competition points, including a pivotal two losing bonus points against the All Blacks, was outstanding. A few top coaches have wondered if this competition makes it harder to blood players, but both France and South Africa have managed to develop depth while winning. The late-blooming lock Verhaeghe – long of limb and deft of hand – is a great example, seizing his opportunity in the summer and then starting throughout this November campaign. Kalvin Gourgues, meanwhile, has carried through his Toulouse form over the last couple of years into the French side as a bundling ball of energy and point of difference in midfield. France are back at closer to full strength (Getty) Even allowing for a few absentees, this French side looks far stronger than when these teams last met a fortnight ago. There will be no trickery with twin scrum halves, with Matthieu Jalibert and Thomas Ramos returning to join Antoine Dupont in probably the world’s best playmaking spine. “We had other options, but this was an obvious decision,” Galthie said of Ramos’ immediate return following injury. The Springboks, for their part, have talked this week of their excitement to take on a French side at closer to full-strength. A side that knows a thing or two about finals

top.title: 100% wear in 15 laps – F1’s tyre challenges in Qatar far more extreme than Pirelli expected
top.description: Motorsport photo Every year, the Lusail International Circuit represents the biggest challenge on the Formula 1 calendar for its sole tyre supplier, Pirelli. It is precisely for that reason that a maximum stint length is once again in place this season, with the limit this time set at 27 laps per set of tyres. The latter was based on Pirelli's pre-event simulations, but in practice, the situation is proving even more extreme than expected, as Pirelli's chief engineer Simone Berra explained. “The point is that the graining level and the wear level are higher than what we expected pre-event. It's quite impressive, the surprises that this circuit gives us every time we come here,” Berra smiled. “What we have noticed is that during the high fuel running, the graining is on all three compounds, C3, C2 and C1. C1 is slightly more resilient in terms of mechanical resistance and the graining level is slightly reduced, while on C2 and C3 the graining level is moderate to heavy. “That is accelerating the wear, mainly in two regions: the TWI 2 and 3 area, so basically towards the inside shoulder of the tyre, and then on the very outside shoulder of the tyre as well. We have two points of high wear and we have seen cases of 100% wear already during the high fuel running after 15 laps.” Those cases of extreme localised wear occurred well before the prescribed 27-lap limit, meaning Pirelli is evaluating whether that limit needs to be reduced further. However, the answer is not necessarily yes, given that, in addition to the wear, tyre degradation is also proving higher than expected. “We are evaluating all the sets that we have selected from FP1 and FP2. We are going to check them, to section them, and obviously if there is no integrity issue, we will keep the 27 laps. We know that the graining level will reduce for the race and the teams will do much more management to extend the stint length,” Berra explained. “So, if they don't induce any increase in terms of integrity issues, then we can keep the 27 laps. But it's an analysis that is ongoing in our laboratory, so we are going to understand if we continue with 27 or not.” Pirelli team Pirelli team Higher degradation could make the existing limit less of a concern for Pirelli, as Berra does not expect teams to push right up to the permitted limit of 27 laps per set. top.title: Chelsea in a ‘difficult moment’ admits Alonso
top.description: Xabi Alonso admitted Chelsea are in a “difficult moment” as the beleaguered boss urged his struggling side to stick together after their dismal 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest on Friday. Alonso’s side crashed to a third successive Premier League loss to leave them languishing in eighth place. The Blues have lost four of their last five league matches, piling pressure on Alonso just months into his reign at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea fell behind to Igor Jesus’s early opener before Morgan Gibbs-White doubled Forest’s lead with a second half penalty. Emmanuel Emegha reduced the deficit but Gibbs-White struck again to make Emega’s late second nothing more than a footnote on another dispiriting evening for Alonso. “It’s a difficult moment for everyone. It’s disappointing again to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions, we can’t stop,” Alonso said. “We are low in confidence, the team is struggling to hold a result. After getting to 2-1 we have conceded and go to 3-1. “Everything is not going our way, we are responsible for that and we are responsible to find solutions.” Chelsea have already conceded 23 goals in 12 league matches and their porous defence was not helped by Alonso’s curious decision to use Ecuador midfielder Moises Caicedo in a back-three. Alonso also selected Wesley Fofana after the centre-back was forced to apologise for joking in a YouTube interview about missing a penalty during Chelsea’s League Cup defeat against Liverpool this season. The hapless Fofana was booed by angry Chelsea fans at the City Ground and conceded a penalty with his careless foul on former Blues striker Liam Delap. “We need to support everyone. Everyone that is in the team we need to support,” Alonso said of Fofana. “We know we have to go through difficult moments. We don’t take apart anyone and we want to help.” Asked to assess Chelsea’s dismal run, Alonso suggested the only cure was hard work on the training ground. “We can do better for sure. At this level you need to hold results and that is why we are losing in the last games,” he said after Chelsea’s sixth league defeat his term. “That is the only way I understand football. When things are not going well, try to work and find solutions. It can happen that we turn it around and it goes our way.” Chelsea’s sixth league defeat under Alonso will spark pointed questions about the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. Although Alonso led Leverkusen to an historic Bundesliga title in 2024, he lasted just seven months before being sacked by Real. The former Liverpool midfielder desperately needs a win against bottom of the table Crystal Palace on Wednesday to avoid the sack talk growing even louder. “Everyone needs to stick together and go through this moment. top.title: Ten live bets, zero accumulators: the story of a bettor from Burkina Faso
top.description: No bets on impulse. No chasing miracles. An AfroPari player from Burkina Faso has made a net profit of over 14 millions $ from ten bets, all placed live. Her idea? While everyone else waits for goals, she bets there won’t be many. One match, one slip Her biggest win: over 6,800 $ on a match in Switzerland Plenty of bettors stuff their slips with five, six, even ten events, dreaming of a huge payout, but not her: one event, sensible odds. Betting on silence She watches the game, feels the tempo, and only then makes her move. She’s after tight, cagey matches where nobody wants to take risks. Most of her bets are on goals staying under a certain line, sometimes in the first half only. Best example? Hoffenheim vs Schalke 04. She backed this one twice: first the first half, then the full match. Two bets, two hits. Not just Europe, not just football Big names aren’t her thing. Europe’s top leagues, yes, but also Colombia, Hong Kong and even ice hockey. It doesn’t matter who’s playing. What matters is how the game is going. An approach, not a recipe You could look at her ten slips and see a method worth copying. It isn’t one. It’s simply how she lives the game: patience, attention, one bet at a time. And nothing was settled in advance: a last-minute goal, a penalty, a defensive slip – and everything could have turned. Above all, her story shows you don’t have to chase big odds. top.title: Bruno Fernandes replacement? Mauricio Pochettino turns to Man Utd's forgotten French wonderkid as injury crisis deepens ahead of Old Trafford debut
top.description: Enzo Kana-Biyik Manchester United - Getty Mauricio Pochettino is wasting no time in exploring the depth of his Manchester United squad as he prepares for his first Premier League home game at Old Trafford. With several senior stars sidelined, the Argentine coach has turned to the club's youth ranks to bolster his options for the visit of Brentford. Pochettino promotes academy prospects for Friday training Enzo Kana-Biyik joined Manchester United's senior group for Friday's training session as head coach Pochettino dealt with multiple absences ahead of Saturday's Premier League fixture against Brentford. The 19-year-old French forward trained alongside fellow academy prospects Jack Fletcher, Tyler Fletcher, Jim Thwaites, and Jaydan Kamason. Captain Bruno Fernandes sat out the session through illness , adding to a growing unavailable list that already includes Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba, and Manuel Ugarte. Pochettino did receive one welcome boost, however, with defender Leny Yoro cleared to play after his red card against Liverpool was overturned on appeal. The Philadelphia Phillies were reportedly interested in Jazz Chisholm Jr. before the infielder ultimately agreed to a contract with the Toronto Blue Jays . top.title: Real Madrid could yet welcome back former academy star as future remains undecided
top.description: Real Madrid could yet welcome back former academy star as future remains undecided Nico Paz remains one of the talk of the town in the world of football, and his start to the new season with Como has been absolutely phenomenal. A Real Madrid academy star for a long time, the player left the club looking for regular minutes and found a convenient project to pioneer under Cesc Fabregas in Serie A. His growth at the club has been astronomical; Real Madrid have monitored his situation closely. The club are seriously considering triggering their buy-back clause on him next summer regardless of the cost, but recent reports have highlighted that Paz is still not convinced about the role he will have under Jose Mourinho. Decision not made Paz has not ruled out a Real Madrid return. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images) As opposed to reports earlier in the week that Paz is against a return , Fabrizio Romano now reports and ‘guarantees’ that the player has not yet made his final decision. The player wants to understand Real Madrid’s plans, project and where they see him fitting into the puzzle before he makes a binding decision. He has not yet decided to officially close the door for Real Madrid, and everything will depend on what the club transmit to him. As matters stand, there is still a chance that Paz will arrive in Madrid next summer. A valid concern The directness with which Paz has handled his career decisions so far is inspiring, for he never allowed the allure of playing for Real Madrid to affect his development. All Nico Paz asks for is a guarantee for minutes. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Throughout his journey, the player’s priority has been regular minutes – something which he earned in abundance on loan and furthered his development. As the door to return to Real Madrid opens one last time, he still continues to approach the situation pragmatically and is asking all the right questions. With Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler already providing in-house solutions for Real Madrid’s attacking midfield, there is seemingly no place for Paz to fit into the XI. If Real Madrid indeed wish to bring Paz back, that is the problem they must look to solve. After all, the player has been open to a return for a long time, and it is only the lack of guaranteed playing time that has inhibited the transfer.

top.title: Relief for Barça Atletic as key duo return in time for top-spot clash against Terrassa
top.description: Relief for Barça Atletic as key duo return in time for top-spot clash against Terrassa Barça Atletic have received a timely boost ahead of Saturday’s crucial Segunda RFEF meeting with Terrassa, with Hamza Abdelkarim and Pedro Villar recovering from injuries and expected to return to the squad, reports Mundo Deportivo . Notably, the match at the Estadi Johan Cruyff carries major significance in the Group 2 promotion race. Hamza Abdelkarim and Pedro Villar return from injury Abdelkarim, 18, has recovered from muscle discomfort that kept him out for the past two weeks. Hamza Abdelkarim’s recovery will be great news for the youth team. Pedro Villar, meanwhile, has also completed his recovery after spending two months out with an injury to the biceps femoris in his left leg. The 18-year-old central midfielder had featured in four matches before suffering the injury during the 4-0 win over Pena Sport. Pedro Villar will be available against Terrassa. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) Both players have trained without problems in the build-up to Terrassa’s visit and are expected to be included in the squad. Their exact minutes remain uncertain, particularly after their respective spells on the sidelines. Belletti faces selection challenge with 11 players unavailable The return of Hamza and Villar comes as Barça Atletic continue to deal with a significant injury crisis. On that note, the aforementioned outlet confirms Sama Nomoko, Patricio Pacífico, Juan Hernández, Eder Aller, Shane Kluivert, Ibrahim Diarra, Dani Ávila, Juwensley Onstein, Hafiz Gariba, Josué Caicedo and Mirza Catovic remain unavailable. top.description: …Over 200 master keys recovered from suspect By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State Security Network Agency, Amotekun Corps, has arrested a suspected serial housebreaker, identified as Michael Morayo, for allegedly breaking into more than 200 houses across different parts of the state. Morayo was among 13 suspected criminals paraded by the security outfit in Akure, the state capital. He was reportedly arrested in the Ijomu area of Akure. According to the Amotekun Corps, the suspect allegedly operated alone for about six years, breaking into houses and stealing household items, which he subsequently sold through an online marketplace he reportedly established. The security outfit said the suspect maintained an affluent lifestyle, dressed elegantly and spoke politely, making it difficult for people to suspect his alleged criminal activities. It added that he operated a warehouse where he kept stolen items and was meticulous in carrying out his operations. Parading the suspects, the State Commander of Amotekun, Chief Adetunji Adeleye, said Morayo allegedly confessed to breaking into more than 200 houses. Adeleye disclosed that over 200 master keys were recovered from him, explaining that the suspect often gained access to houses without forcing doors or breaking locks. “He does not always break doors to gain access to houses. We recovered well over 200 master keys from him. He also confessed that he usually finds ways of visiting people under different pretences. “In the process, he checks their doors and, while engaging them in conversation, removes one of their spare keys,” Adeleye said. He advised residents against keeping multiple keys in their door locks, warning that the practice could expose their homes to burglars. According to him, the suspect sometimes allegedly removed keys from doors and kept them in his pocket to gain access to the houses later. Adeleye further alleged that Morayo had other methods of gaining entry into homes, including making occupants fall asleep before stealing household equipment. The Amotekun commander said the suspect’s lifestyle and manner of presentation often shielded him from suspicion. He assured that all 13 suspects arrested and paraded by the corps would face prosecution after investigations. “After detailed investigations, they will be charged before courts of competent jurisdiction, depending on the offences they are suspected to have committed,” he said. nigeria.description: There is a slow turnout at polling units 031 and 032 in Ungwan Boro, Sabon Tasha ward, in Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State, as there is little to suggest that the mock accreditation exercise set to hold today by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is taking place. nigeria.title: Chelsea in a ‘difficult moment’ admits Alonso
nigeria.description: Xabi Alonso admitted Chelsea are in a “difficult moment” as the beleaguered boss urged his struggling side to stick together after their dismal 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest on Friday. Alonso’s side crashed to a third successive Premier League loss to leave them languishing in eighth place. The Blues have lost four of their last five league matches, piling pressure on Alonso just months into his reign at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea fell behind to Igor Jesus’s early opener before Morgan Gibbs-White doubled Forest’s lead with a second half penalty. Emmanuel Emegha reduced the deficit but Gibbs-White struck again to make Emega’s late second nothing more than a footnote on another dispiriting evening for Alonso. “It’s a difficult moment for everyone. It’s disappointing again to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions, we can’t stop,” Alonso said. “We are low in confidence, the team is struggling to hold a result. After getting to 2-1 we have conceded and go to 3-1. “Everything is not going our way, we are responsible for that and we are responsible to find solutions.” Chelsea have already conceded 23 goals in 12 league matches and their porous defence was not helped by Alonso’s curious decision to use Ecuador midfielder Moises Caicedo in a back-three. Alonso also selected Wesley Fofana after the centre-back was forced to apologise for joking in a YouTube interview about missing a penalty during Chelsea’s League Cup defeat against Liverpool this season. The hapless Fofana was booed by angry Chelsea fans at the City Ground and conceded a penalty with his careless foul on former Blues striker Liam Delap. “We need to support everyone. Everyone that is in the team we need to support,” Alonso said of Fofana. “We know we have to go through difficult moments. We don’t take apart anyone and we want to help.” Asked to assess Chelsea’s dismal run, Alonso suggested the only cure was hard work on the training ground. “We can do better for sure. At this level you need to hold results and that is why we are losing in the last games,” he said after Chelsea’s sixth league defeat his term. “That is the only way I understand football. When things are not going well, try to work and find solutions. It can happen that we turn it around and it goes our way.” Chelsea’s sixth league defeat under Alonso will spark pointed questions about the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. Although Alonso led Leverkusen to an historic Bundesliga title in 2024, he lasted just seven months before being sacked by Real. The former Liverpool midfielder desperately needs a win against bottom of the table Crystal Palace on Wednesday to avoid the sack talk growing even louder. “Everyone needs to stick together and go through this moment. nigeria.title: Ten live bets, zero accumulators: the story of a bettor from Burkina Faso
nigeria.description: No bets on impulse. No chasing miracles. An AfroPari player from Burkina Faso has made a net profit of over 14 millions $ from ten bets, all placed live. Her idea? While everyone else waits for goals, she bets there won’t be many. One match, one slip Her biggest win: over 6,800 $ on a match in Switzerland Plenty of bettors stuff their slips with five, six, even ten events, dreaming of a huge payout, but not her: one event, sensible odds. Betting on silence She watches the game, feels the tempo, and only then makes her move. She’s after tight, cagey matches where nobody wants to take risks. Most of her bets are on goals staying under a certain line, sometimes in the first half only. Best example? Hoffenheim vs Schalke 04. She backed this one twice: first the first half, then the full match. Two bets, two hits. Not just Europe, not just football Big names aren’t her thing. Europe’s top leagues, yes, but also Colombia, Hong Kong and even ice hockey. It doesn’t matter who’s playing. What matters is how the game is going. An approach, not a recipe You could look at her ten slips and see a method worth copying. It isn’t one. It’s simply how she lives the game: patience, attention, one bet at a time. And nothing was settled in advance: a last-minute goal, a penalty, a defensive slip – and everything could have turned. Above all, her story shows you don’t have to chase big odds. nigeria.title: A Weekend For Proof
nigeria.description: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. That development changes the context of the coming days. Electoral preparation now requires visible progress on protection, accountability and public confidence alongside equipment and political agreements. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. It will test accreditation, election devices, and the uploading and viewing of simulated results. Registered voters in the selected units are expected to participate. The most useful outcome would be a public account of performance. How many locations opened on time? How many participants were successfully accredited? Where did devices fail? How long did uploads take? How were exceptions resolved? A rehearsal can reveal problems that announcements cannot. Finding a fault early allows INEC to correct it. Explaining that correction gives citizens a reason to have greater confidence. The exercise also has practical support from state governments. Lagos has cancelled Saturday’s sanitation exercise, while Anambra has postponed its own, to avoid obstructing participation. Those decisions remove an immediate obstacle. The remaining test concerns delivery at the selected polling units. Monday: What Will Opposition Unity Require? Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Seyi Makinde and other opposition leaders are expected at the November 30 summit. Their attendance and any signed commitments remain forthcoming. The APC says it is untroubled by the proposed gathering. The parties’ task is to define cooperation precisely. Joint election monitoring could be valuable. So could common procedures for documenting intimidation, sharing verified information and coordinating legal responses. Presidential cooperation presents more difficult choices. Supporters need to know whether their parties intend to campaign separately, endorse an existing candidate or pursue another lawful arrangement. A declaration of unity leaves those questions open unless it specifies obligations.

nigeria.title: Trump proposes new tariffs on China, EU, 12 others
nigeria.description: By Vera Anyagafu US President Donald Trump has proposed a new round of tariffs on 14 major trading partners, including China and the European Union. The proposals were announced on Wednesday, November 25, by the Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR) after an eight-month investigation into what Washington calls ‘structural excess capacity’. The US says the targeted countries are promoting production through subsidies and other industrial policies, allowing them to flood world markets with cheap goods and undercut American manufacturers. The 14 economies targeted are China, Bangladesh, Cambodia, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam. Mexico and Norway were also investigated but have been spared for now. China faces a proposed rate of 20 per cent on most products, which would be added to tariffs imposed during Trump’s first term, but would not stack on top of more recent forced-labour tariffs. According to a senior US official, the rate could double to 40 per cent if talks between Washington and Beijing fall apart. Products from the EU will be taxed at 15 per cent in compliance with the US deal with the bloc, though USTR said that could also rise to as much as 20 per cent. The new tariffs are being proposed under Section 301 of the 1974 US Trade Act, which allows Washington to penalise countries it determines are treating US businesses unfairly. The proposals are still subject to a public comment process, with comments closing on January 5, 2027, and a public hearing starting January 25, 2027, before any final action. However, Beijing has rejected the accusations, with Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun saying the so-called overcapacity is a false issue, and China opposes using it as an excuse for political manipulation. Also present at the service were African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain, Dino Melaye, and an aide to Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori. The service, held at the church’s Glory Dome, formed part of activities marking the 30th anniversary of Dunamis, founded in November 1996 by Pastor Paul Enenche and his wife, Becky, both medical doctors turned pastors. The prayer points included a plea for God’s perfect will to prevail in Nigeria, and for the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to conduct the 2027 elections fairly. The congregation also prayed for the smooth functioning of electoral systems and equipment, including the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), as well as reliable internet connectivity during the elections. They further prayed for credible elections without bloodshed, crisis or post-election violence. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. sports.title: Doctor’s coat takes backseat as Maha’s Vedika Magar chases cricket dreams for Sikkim
sports.description: MUMBAI: Not many would give up a settled career, especially one as a doctor, to pursue a sporting dream. Vedika Magar did just that to follow her passion for cricket. Last month, she took her first step towards realising that dream when she represented Sikkim in the Senior Women’s T20 Trophy. Her next target is to play for Mumbai. She has featured on the state’s probables list for the past three seasons but is yet to make the Mumbai 15. Vedika had always wanted to be a cricketer. However, lack of facilities in her hometown of Pandharpur meant that her opportunities were limited to playing tennis-ball cricket with boys in her neighbourhood. When it came to choosing between an engineering seat in Pune and a medical seat in Mumbai, she opted for the latter and enrolled at Grant Medical College. She arrived in Mumbai at 17, fell in love with the city and rediscovered her passion for cricket. In college, she first bowled with a leather ball while practising with the boys’ team. She later began training at the nets of the late Vidya Paradkar, a well-known coach on Mumbai’s maidans, at Cross Maidan. It was only after completing her internship that she was encouraged to take cricket seriously. “Dr Hemant Gupta, who worked in the department of medicine at JJ Hospital, saw me play and was impressed. He was the one who helped me find a club in the city,” the 26-yearold said. At 23, Vedika put her plans for postgraduate studies on hold and took up a job at JJ Hospital to continue her cricketing journey. Her efforts paid off when she made Mumbai’s list of 30 probables for the first time in 2024. “Juggling night shifts, training and matches took a toll on me. I had calcium deficiency and my health deteriorated,” recalls the left-arm spinner. She eventually had to choose between her job and cricket. This time, with her parents’ support, she chose the game.She also landed a role as team doctor with Delhi Capitals’ Women’s Premier League (WPL) outfit. The job helped her manage her expenses while giving her an opportunity to interact with top players and observe their preparation. But progress on the field remained elusive. Then, while browsing the web, she came across an advertisement for open trials for Sikkim. She decided to give it a shot and was rewarded with selection.

sports.title: The ‘extra spice’ fuelling France vs South Africa showdown in Nations Championship final
sports.description: It is, in the words of a rival head coach, a “fitting final”. Andy Farrell did not hide his disappointment that Ireland did not make the inaugural Nations Championship showpiece but he did not dispute that France and South Africa were worthy combatants for the trophy. Asked to assess their relative strengths and make a prediction following his side’s win over Australia , the Ireland head coach spent several minutes explaining what makes each so good before eventually suggesting it was too close to call. “But isn’t that how it should be?” Farrell asked – indeed, Andy, indeed. This format clearly has its challenges but there is hope of a dazzling denouement. These are the reigning champions of the northern and southern hemispheres, however distant the Springboks ’ success in last year’s Rugby Championship now feels. Their recent encounter of fine margins in Paris has only deepened a rivalry that has festered in the last half-decade. “I find that it's a good challenge to play them twice in a row knowing that we have already beaten them the first time,” the France lock Florian Verhaeghe said. “That adds a little extra spice.” Florian Verhaeghe believes there will be ‘extra spice’ in the final (Getty) France, by rights, should not really be here. As detailed previously , they were more ambivalent than most towards the Nations Championship, with the July Test window generally considered secondary to the Top 14 climax that almost directly precedes it. Though Bordeaux Begles’ surprise failure to make the play-offs bolstered his options somewhat, head coach Fabien Galthie was still without a raft of regulars for fixtures against New Zealand, Australia and Japan in the first phase of this tournament; to come away with 12 competition points, including a pivotal two losing bonus points against the All Blacks, was outstanding. A few top coaches have wondered if this competition makes it harder to blood players, but both France and South Africa have managed to develop depth while winning. The late-blooming lock Verhaeghe – long of limb and deft of hand – is a great example, seizing his opportunity in the summer and then starting throughout this November campaign. Kalvin Gourgues, meanwhile, has carried through his Toulouse form over the last couple of years into the French side as a bundling ball of energy and point of difference in midfield. France are back at closer to full strength (Getty) Even allowing for a few absentees, this French side looks far stronger than when these teams last met a fortnight ago. There will be no trickery with twin scrum halves, with Matthieu Jalibert and Thomas Ramos returning to join Antoine Dupont in probably the world’s best playmaking spine. “We had other options, but this was an obvious decision,” Galthie said of Ramos’ immediate return following injury. sports.description: Motorsport photo Every year, the Lusail International Circuit represents the biggest challenge on the Formula 1 calendar for its sole tyre supplier, Pirelli. It is precisely for that reason that a maximum stint length is once again in place this season, with the limit this time set at 27 laps per set of tyres. The latter was based on Pirelli's pre-event simulations, but in practice, the situation is proving even more extreme than expected, as Pirelli's chief engineer Simone Berra explained. “The point is that the graining level and the wear level are higher than what we expected pre-event. It's quite impressive, the surprises that this circuit gives us every time we come here,” Berra smiled. “What we have noticed is that during the high fuel running, the graining is on all three compounds, C3, C2 and C1. C1 is slightly more resilient in terms of mechanical resistance and the graining level is slightly reduced, while on C2 and C3 the graining level is moderate to heavy. “That is accelerating the wear, mainly in two regions: the TWI 2 and 3 area, so basically towards the inside shoulder of the tyre, and then on the very outside shoulder of the tyre as well. We have two points of high wear and we have seen cases of 100% wear already during the high fuel running after 15 laps.” Those cases of extreme localised wear occurred well before the prescribed 27-lap limit, meaning Pirelli is evaluating whether that limit needs to be reduced further. However, the answer is not necessarily yes, given that, in addition to the wear, tyre degradation is also proving higher than expected. “We are evaluating all the sets that we have selected from FP1 and FP2. We are going to check them, to section them, and obviously if there is no integrity issue, we will keep the 27 laps. We know that the graining level will reduce for the race and the teams will do much more management to extend the stint length,” Berra explained. “So, if they don't induce any increase in terms of integrity issues, then we can keep the 27 laps. But it's an analysis that is ongoing in our laboratory, so we are going to understand if we continue with 27 or not.” Pirelli team Pirelli team Higher degradation could make the existing limit less of a concern for Pirelli, as Berra does not expect teams to push right up to the permitted limit of 27 laps per set. The Philadelphia Phillies were reportedly interested in Jazz Chisholm Jr. before the infielder ultimately agreed to a contract with the Toronto Blue Jays . The two-time All-Star ultimately signed a one-year, $20 million deal with Toronto that includes options for the future. According to MLB insider Robert Murray, the Phillies and San Diego Padres were among the teams interested in Chisholm before he chose the Blue Jays. The contract includes a $6 million signing bonus, a $12.5 million salary for 2027, and a $16 million player option with a $1.5 million buyout. It will become a $40 million club option if Chisholm decides to decline the player option. Chisholm is coming off a relatively underwhelming season with the New York Yankees. He hit .231 with 19 home runs, 55 RBIs and a .711 OPS while stealing a career-high 41 bases. However, his 2025 campaign was considerably stronger, as he finished with 31 home runs, 80 RBIs and an .813 OPS. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Phillies could have explored Chisholm as an infield or outfield option. However, his natural position is second base, where Philadelphia already has Bryson Stott. Chisholm also has experience in the outfield but struggled defensively in center field during his time with the Miami Marlins and Yankees. Philadelphia manager Don Mattingly also has experience working with Chisholm, having managed him in Miami from 2020 to 2022. Mattingly previously praised the infielder’s confidence and approach at the plate. “Jazz is Jazz. He’s himself,” Mattingly said in 2024. “I love Jazz just from the standpoint of I think he’s fearless. sports.title: Real Madrid could yet welcome back former academy star as future remains undecided
sports.description: Real Madrid could yet welcome back former academy star as future remains undecided Nico Paz remains one of the talk of the town in the world of football, and his start to the new season with Como has been absolutely phenomenal. A Real Madrid academy star for a long time, the player left the club looking for regular minutes and found a convenient project to pioneer under Cesc Fabregas in Serie A. His growth at the club has been astronomical; Real Madrid have monitored his situation closely. The club are seriously considering triggering their buy-back clause on him next summer regardless of the cost, but recent reports have highlighted that Paz is still not convinced about the role he will have under Jose Mourinho. Decision not made Paz has not ruled out a Real Madrid return. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images) As opposed to reports earlier in the week that Paz is against a return , Fabrizio Romano now reports and ‘guarantees’ that the player has not yet made his final decision. The player wants to understand Real Madrid’s plans, project and where they see him fitting into the puzzle before he makes a binding decision. He has not yet decided to officially close the door for Real Madrid, and everything will depend on what the club transmit to him. As matters stand, there is still a chance that Paz will arrive in Madrid next summer. A valid concern The directness with which Paz has handled his career decisions so far is inspiring, for he never allowed the allure of playing for Real Madrid to affect his development. All Nico Paz asks for is a guarantee for minutes. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Throughout his journey, the player’s priority has been regular minutes – something which he earned in abundance on loan and furthered his development. As the door to return to Real Madrid opens one last time, he still continues to approach the situation pragmatically and is asking all the right questions. sports.description: “It’s not bad getting a compliment like that" – Bischof on Gerrard praise Tom Bischof has been pushed into a prominent role this season under Vincent Kompany and has been making waves both in Germany and abroad. The 21-year-old put in a top performance in October as a rotated Bayern side earned a 2-2 draw with Arsenal. “It was a great game," Bischof said in an interview with the DFL. "If we’d won it in the end, it would’ve been an even greater game. But it was also cool for me to see and to start at such a top level." Bischof completed 96% of his 54 passes against Mikel Arteta's side while also covering the most distance of any player on the pitch. Bischof and Aleksandar Pavlović held their own against a top midfield consisting of Declan Rice and Bruno Guimarães. After the match, the duo earned praise from legendary Liverpool midfielder Steven Gerrard for their performances, with the ex-England international stating he was “really impressed” by both. The praise has not gone unnoticed. “My friends sent it to me and I was obviously aware of it and read it a couple of times, because it makes you happy and is a proud moment having that feeling," Bischof said. "So you’re always happy about it.” Gerrard is not the only Liverpool legend that Bischof has impressed. The youngster has been a regular under new coach Jürgen Klopp for Germany, appearing in four consecutive matches. Germany has won three of the four. “I think he’s just like you expect – the way he gets players on board,” Bischof said. “I’m very convinced of him and think he’ll lead us down a good path.” With Bayern depleted by injuries, and Germany looking to refresh the squad, the 21-year-old should continue to get ample opportunities for both. Still, while on an individual level, he is having a strong season, but there is more work to be done. Bayern are heading into their final six matches of 2026 in mixed form. Among those is a rematch with TSG Hoffenheim, the club where Bischof got his start. Much has changed since he left Hoffenheim in 2025, and the midfielder has gone from strength to strength. Even with Bischof now performing in the Champions League at Bayern, he's looking to continue improving. “It’s not bad getting a compliment like that from Steven Gerrard,” Bischof said. "It makes me happy, but I want to build on my performance from that game and just keep going.”

sports.title: 3 Takeaways as Stephon Castle keys Spurs' NBA Cup comeback
sports.description: San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) embraces San Antonio Spurs forward Carter Bryant (11) in an NBA Cup game at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. The Spurs defeated the Lakers 99-96. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) With the Spurs in the throes of one of their most thrilling comebacks of the season, the ball found Stephon Castle in the left corner late Friday night. He didn't need much time to decide what to do with it. "I'm just trying to get the best shot available," Castle said. As it turned out, the best shot available was the one in his hands. Castle's corner 3-pointer with 43.4 seconds remaining gave the Spurs some much-needed breathing room in what became a 99-96 victory over the Los Angeles Lakers in a do-or-die NBA Cup showdown at the Frost Bank Center. "I had the shot," Castle said, "so I took it." Castle and Victor Wembanyama teamed up to win an MVP-caliber duel against Luka Doncic and the Los Angeles Lakers, one that punched the Spurs ticket into the NBA Cup knockout rounds. The Spurs face Dallas on Friday at the American Airlines Center. Getting there required the Spurs to dig themselves out of a hole they had spent the first half making. Castle finished with 26 points - including a late 3-pointer that put the Spurs ahead 96-90 - while Wembanyama piled up 25 points, 16 rebounds, two blocks and four steals. San Antonio Spurs guard Stephon Castle (5) hits a drum after the team defeated the Los Angeles Lakers 99-96 in an NBA Cup game at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) Doncic cooled after a sizzling start, ending with 31 points but needing 31 shot attempts to get there. Playing in his first game since suffering a heel injury Nov. 11, Austin Reaves rejoined the L.A. lineup and chipped in 21 points. To stay alive in the NBA Cup field, the Spurs had to overcome their worst first quarter (14 points) and first half (38 points) of the season. The Spurs fell behind by as many as 20 points before intermission. "We got punked in the first half," Spurs forward Carter Bryant said. The Spurs trimmed their deficit to 58-34 at the break, then turned the tables on the Lakers after halftime. A 30-14 third quarter pulled the Spurs into a 68-all tie headed to the fourth, where they did just enough to pull out the victory. "We might have been dominated in the first half," Wembanyama said. "We dominated more than they did in the second half." The Spurs improved to 16-4, surpassing the Lakers (15-4) for the top record in the Western Conference. Here are three takeaways from Friday's victory: 1. Finally, Spurs have a signature win Heading into Friday's showdown with the NBA-leading Lakers, the Spurs had posted a 9-0 record against teams with a sub-.500 record. They were 6-4 against teams with winning records. Their four losses, meanwhile, had come against the best four teams they had faced - Oklahoma City, Houston, Detroit and Portland.

sports.title: Inside story of how Marc Casado’s loan move from Barcelona to Deportivo was pulled off on deadline day
sports.description: Inside story of how Marc Casado’s loan move from Barcelona to Deportivo was pulled off on deadline day Barcelona had decided last summer that Marc Casado needed to leave in search of regular football, but the club initially preferred a permanent transfer rather than a loan. This is because the midfielder attracted financially attractive offers from Saudi Arabia and interest from Turkish clubs, yet he prioritised continuing his career in Spain and remaining in European football. Furthermore, the Blaugrana’s €30 million valuation proved a major obstacle, but that was understandable because Casado still had two years left on his contract and was reluctant to sever his connection with the club where he had developed since joining La Masia in 2016. Notably, Deportivo’s proposal only gained momentum late in the window . The La Liga club’s ambitious project, including the arrivals of former Barcelona players Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Adama Traore, appealed to Casado, who was keen to find a sporting environment where he could play regularly. Deportivo’s late approach nearly collapsed Deportivo have a non-mandatory €30 million purchase option for Marc Casado. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) According to SPORT , Deportivo moved quickly enough to arrange a flight for Casado to A Coruna, but the midfielder remained in Barcelona after disagreements between the clubs prevented the deal from being completed. The negotiations continued into the final day of the transfer window. Barcelona wanted to protect their financial interests, while Deportivo needed an agreement that could fit within its economic limitations. Casado’s representative, Jorge Mendes, and the clubs’ legal teams remained involved as the parties worked through the final details. The result was a season-long loan with a non-mandatory €30 million purchase option, giving Deportivo the opportunity to sign him permanently without an obligation to do so. The agreement was completed five minutes before the deadline Deportivo wasn’t the most favourable transfer for Casado. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As per the outlet, the verbal agreement between Barcelona and Deportivo was reached at approximately 11pm. The remaining legal procedures were completed electronically, allowing Casado to be registered just five minutes before the transfer window closed. Barcelona’s official announcement confirmed that the midfielder would spend the season at Deportivo until June 30, 2027. Put together, the late agreement was a compromise for all parties , as Barcelona avoided losing the player without a transfer arrangement, Deportivo secured a midfielder for its return to the top flight, and Casado found a route to regular football while keeping the possibility of returning to his boyhood club open.

sports.title: 'We must improve quickly!' - Jordan Henderson lays blame on 'sloppy' Chelsea stars after Nottingham Forest defensive horror show
sports.description: Nottingham Forest FC v Chelsea FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Jordan Henderson has delivered a scathing assessment of Chelsea’s defensive standards following their disappointing 3-2 defeat to Nottingham Forest. The veteran midfielder insisted the Blues were the architects of their own downfall at the City Ground as they struggled to maintain concentration against their hosts. Slow starts cost Blues at the City Ground Nottingham Forest punished Chelsea inside the opening five minutes of both halves, leaving the visitors chasing deficits of 2-0 and 3-1 before they found any attacking rhythm. Emmanuel Emegha struck twice to spark a late fightback as Forest dropped deeper to protect their lead, yet the Blues ran out of time to rescue a point . Henderson laments preventable goals and late urgency Speaking after the final whistle, Henderson did not hide his frustration over how easily Forest breached Chelsea's backline early in each period. "The goals we conceded were sloppy," the former Liverpool captain told Chelsea's official website . "We are disappointed with that first and foremost. I think the three goals we can stop them, so we are really disappointed with that. "For some reason they had a couple of half-decent chances, and they scored. The first five minutes of the first half, the first five minutes of the second half, so we are disappointed with the goals we have conceded for sure." The veteran midfielder also noted that Chelsea only showed real urgency once Forest retreated to defend their cushion. He added: "We didn't get going until they were 2-0 up or 3-1 up, when they started to drop deep and we started to get the ball forward a bit quicker. "Obviously we kept going and we got a couple of goals. We were pushing in the last few minutes of the game to try and get an equaliser. We kept going right until the end, which was a positive, but overall we can still play better and be better. Defensively, we need to improve quickly." Whole squad must share defensive burden Rather than singling out the backline, Henderson framed the defeat as a collective failure, warning that lapses in concentration have become a recurring problem across the side. "We need to solve it as a team. It is not just about the defence, it is about the whole team defending as one to stop conceding chances and goals," he continued. "In the main, did I think they had a lot of chances? Not really. But the chances we gave away, we conceded goals, and that seems to be the way it is at the minute. We need to be on it every single minute of the game, with concentration and focus. "There are still some positives to take, but overall we need to be better. Playing for Chelsea, we need to be coming here and putting in better performances." technology.title: Unkernel and Trynix just transported computing to 2035
technology.description: What's the difference between just-for-fun demo hacks, and serious carefully designed large-scale software architecture? It's the quick-and-dirty jobs that end up transforming computing. A blog post earlier this week called 2035 came early led the Reg FOSS desk down what we thought was a fascinating, and possibly quite scary, rabbit-hole… but it turned out to be an entire warren. We thought we were still in 2026, but in turns out that in some ways, tech just leaped forward a decade. To try to convey the point of this blog post – why what had been just a fun clever little hack has the potential to take half a century of OS and hypervisor design and throw it out of the nearest window – will take quite a lot of unpacking. If you bear with us, we will try to walk you through it. To get started, we need to go back a decade or more. Stick with this: there are laughs, as well as hammers taken to beloved ideas. The year of 2035 and the ideas around that come from a remarkable talk by Gary Bernhardt of Destroy All Software, which is both funny and highly educational. It will really massively assist understanding what this article and the technology is all about if you have the time to watch the talks. The Reg FOSS desk is not at all fond of spoken-word video as a medium – we much prefer to read than listen – but the three talks we're going to mention are golden, among the very best presentations this century in all of computing and IT. Seriously, they are worth your time. As a preface, before we go into Bernhardt's half-hour information-dense talk, let's warm up with a four-minute funny one. But first, let's look at the context for that. Step 0: JavaScript is the language of web programming In 2009, Jeff Atwood laid this out in an article called All Programming is Web Programming . It's still coming true today. Software is getting very blurred around the edges. The entire SaaS industry means that massive organizations run on web apps. Tech like Electron embeds a web browser inside JavaScript apps built in Node.js, while Progressive Web Apps make websites look like local program windows. The most popular desktop Linux in the world is ChromeOS Flex, which doesn't support local native applications at all. Everything is browser windows, even the desktop. It's all built in JavaScript. And yet… Step 1: JavaScript is kind of weird and kind of bad. Bernhardt made this case in 2012, with a celebrated lightning talk called Wat , from the CodeMash conference in 2012. Wat walks through a whole list of examples of how JavaScript is a very strange programming language and does very strange things that are not at all what you might expect. Some of the jokes will make more sense to programmers, but we reckon anyone who has ever fought with a recalcitrant bit of software will get some laughs from it – and that probably applies to all readers of The Register. Step 2: JavaScript is in the process of conquering the world. Bernhardt moved on to much bigger ideas at PyCon 2014

technology.title: Smartphone shipments face another bleak year before modest 2028 comeback
technology.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery.
